synopsis: Project Chrono is a free, BSD-3 open-source dynamics engine for wheeled, tracked and articulated vehicles, with rigid terrain and SCM, CRM and DEM deformable-terrain models; release 10.0.0 is dated 27 March 2026 [f15907, f8493, f8494, f8496]. Its off-road research relevance includes military and planetary mobility, NATO mobility benchmarks, and listed users including US Army organizations, NREL and JPL [f8675, f4164, f8497]. SCM authors claim empirical-model speed with fidelity comparable to discrete element methods, whereas higher-fidelity CRM runs 50–200 times slower than real time and requires an NVIDIA GPU, motivating selective use to calibrate lower-order models rather than every regression case [f6097, f8499, f8500, f8584]. Developers warn that Pacejka, TMeasy and Fiala handling tire models do not work on deformable terrain, creating a risk that tool coupling silently breaks the physics [f8498, f8725]. Experimental terrain validation is reported, but documented capabilities do not establish machine-specific emergency stopping-distance accuracy; no common production-machine stopping benchmark was found, and the skeptic chapter did not review Chrono validation literature [f8583, f6016, f6561, f10611]. Chrono is not turnkey test management, qualification-ready coupling to Isaac requires major work, and its 2020 sensor framework left real-sensor validation as future work; low-license-cost integration still carries substantial internal labor, while maintenance funding and security-patch cadence were not examined [f8501, f9280, f4341, f16128, f9392, f9393].
